title: POC decision rubric + evaluation deliverables
summary: AE + SE walked through the proposed acceptance rubric for the POC: functional correctness thresholds, latency/throughput SLOs, cost guardrails, and the reporting format. Customer clarified dataset slices and sensitive-data constraints. Agreed next steps: share benchmark runbook and reporting template; Redwood to provision a short dedicated trial and run baseline noise-free benchmark; security send SOC2 + KMS notes.
next_steps: Maya to share benchmark runbook + spreadsheet by 2025-08-23
Redwood to provision 2 x mid-tier dedicated nodes for 48 hours (week of 2025-08-25) and run baseline suite
Victor + Ben to provide 3 representative prompt sets and 2 labeled evaluation packs by 2025-08-26
Schedule results review + Go/No-Go sync for 2025-08-28 (30m)
Priya to request SOC2 report and confirm KMS/HSM requirements by 2025-08-24
action_items: Maya Patel: Send baseline benchmark spreadsheet, runbook, and pass/fail rubric; Due 2025-08-23
Carlos Nguyen: Prepare dedicated trial config & quickstart script; Due 2025-08-25
Ben Carter: Deliver 3 prompt slices and 2 labeled eval packs (intent+ground truth); Due 2025-08-26
Priya Singh: Confirm encryption at rest policy and whether HSM is required; Due 2025-08-24
Victor Zhao: Confirm success executive metrics and rollout gatekeepers; Due 2025-08-26
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — appreciate you carving time. we'll go through the POC decision rubric and what we'll hand back as deliverables. I'm Maya, AE on the account. Carlos is our solutions engineer.
[00:12] Carlos Nguyen (Redwood SE): hi hi, quick mic check, can you all hear me okay?
[00:16] Victor Zhao: Yep, good here.
[00:18] Lena Morris: Loud and clear.
[00:21] Maya Patel: Cool. Quick agenda: 1) confirm what 'success' looks like for ClearSight, 2) map workload slices and traffic shape, 3) show the benchmark plan (what we'll measure), 4) agree go/no-go thresholds and reporting format, 5) timeline.
[00:35] Carlos Nguyen: I’ll drop in specifics on latencies and the way we run synthetic traffic. note, our runbook uses a mix of playback and live-ish sampling so we can separate cold start vs warmed cache.
[00:45] Victor Zhao: We care about p95 latency under load but also the hallucination/accuracy for our triage prompts. If the model produces wrong diagnoses we'll fail the POC regardless of latency.
[00:57] Priya Singh: For us security is a non-negotiable: data never leaves our VPC during the test, logs must be queryable but redacted for PHI, and key material needs to be customer-managed KMS or HSM.
[01:10] Maya Patel: Understood — VPC/private deployment options and KMS are in scope. we'll include that in the runbook and the acceptance checklist.
[01:20] Lena Morris: On volume — our pilot traffic shape is about 100 concurrent sessions with spikes to 250 for 20 minutes every hour. Avg tokens per request around 400, but there’s a long-tail of 2k tokens for some summarization tasks.
[01:36] Carlos Nguyen: ok that's useful. For sizing we'll recommend a mix: prefer to run the bench with the long-tail turned on for a subset of runs to capture KV cache & memory pressure. note: sometimes our transcriptions show "K-V cash" in auto text, but it's KV cache. just watch for that.
[01:52] Ben Carter: Quick question — do you want production data or synthetically anonymized? We can't share raw PHI.
[01:58] Maya Patel: We'll accept de-identified samples. Ideally you provide the real prompt shape and a de-id sample set plus labeled evals. The acceptance testing will use the labeled eval packs you can provide.
[02:09] Victor Zhao: For accuracy metrics we want: fidelity (precision/recall where applicable), an annotation-based hallucination rate, and a pass/fail rule for critical intents.
[02:20] Carlos Nguyen: That maps well to our standard POC rubric. We typically include three gates: correctness (user-defined thresholds on labeled sets), performance (latency/throughput SLOs under target concurrency), and stability/cost (no more than X% tail variance, and cost per 1M tokens within agreed guardrails).
[02:36] Maya Patel: Let's put numbers on that so folks have something concrete. Proposed thresholds: correctness — >= 92% intent match on labeled pack; hallucination <= 3% on safety-sensitive prompts; performance — p95 inference latency <= 450ms for the 400-token average under 100 concurrent sessions; throughput — sustain 80 qps for the concurrency profile; cost guardrail — baseline cost delta under 20% of your current hosted endpoint cost.
[03:03] Victor Zhao: 450ms p95 is reasonable as a starting point, though borderline. Our product team would prefer 300ms if possible. Could we define a stretch target?
[03:12] Maya Patel: Yes — we can have hard thresholds (go/no-go) and stretch targets. Hard SLO: p95 <= 450ms. Stretch: p95 <= 300ms. We'll put both in the report.
[03:22] Priya Singh: On the correctness side, how do you handle determinism vs sampling? Some of our use cases rely on deterministic outputs for triage.
[03:30] Carlos Nguyen: We run both modes: temperature 0 for deterministic tests, and temperature 0.7 for representative user-facing samples. The eval pack should include labeled examples for both modes. We'll report separate metrics.
[03:43] Ben Carter: For the benchmark runs, which model variants will we use? We want to see an open model and a Redwood-optimized variant.
[03:49] Carlos Nguyen: We'll propose 2-3 variants: the base open model you prefer (e.g., LlamaX-33b), Redwood-optimized quantized run, and a lower-cost scaled variant. We'll run all variants through the same suite and surface tradeoffs.
[04:02] Lena Morris: Good. What about logging and reporting format — we need a single-page exec summary plus a tech appendix.
[04:09] Maya Patel: Agreed. Our standard deliverable: 1) Executive one-pager with go/no-go verdict and summary metrics, 2) Benchmark spreadsheet (per-prompt results, latency distributions, resource utilization), 3) Runbook with steps to reproduce, and 4) Optional recording of the benchmark run and infra config.
[04:26] Victor Zhao: For the go/no-go decision — who signs off from ClearSight? Victor: CTO. Lena: MLOps. Priya: security gates. We'll need the final report to highlight which gate failed if it's a no-go.
[04:38] Maya Patel: We'll include a decision rubric table in the report that maps each metric to owner and pass/fail logic.
[04:44] [00:04:45] Speaker 1: mhm, yeah.
[04:46] Carlos Nguyen: On measurement specifics — we sample p50/p90/p95/p99 latencies, memory and GPU utilization, cold-start contribution (first token), and token-generation throughput. We'll also track model quality via BLEU/ROUGE where applicable and task-specific accuracy.
[05:02] Priya Singh: About audit logs — we need redactable logs and a retention policy. Do you support per-request redaction and a way to query logs without returning PHI?
[05:12] Maya Patel: Yes — Redwood Console supports token-level redaction flags and export filters. we'll share an appendix describing log retention options and SAML/SSO integration steps.
[05:24] Victor Zhao: Another practical constraint: our scheduled internal demo is on 2025-09-02, so we need final POC verdict by 2025-08-29 to give the product team time.
[05:33] Maya Patel: ok — we’ll tighten the timeline. Proposed schedule we discussed: run baselines week of 8/25, run labeled evals as soon as you hand them over, results review 8/28, final sign-off 8/29.
[05:43] Lena Morris: Are you able to run a noisy multi-tenant scenario? We want to understand worst-case degradation when other customers spike.
[05:49] Carlos Nguyen: yes, we can simulate cross-tenant noisy traffic to surface tail behavior. We'll clearly mark those runs as stress tests distinct from baseline runs.
[05:57] Ben Carter: For the labeled eval packs — do you accept CSV with prompt, expected_output, and tolerance fields?
[06:03] Carlos Nguyen: CSV is fine. Prefer column names: prompt_id, prompt_text, expected_text, match_type (exact/contains), tolerance_score. We'll emit a template in the runbook.
[06:16] [00:06:17] Speaker 2: okay cool.
[06:18] Priya Singh: On encryption at rest — we require customer-managed keys. If HSM is required, what's the lead time?
[06:25] Maya Patel: HSM integration is possible but depends on your KMS vendor. We'll capture the option in the security appendix and estimate lead time; typically a few weeks for enterprise setups, but for the POC we can run a scoped test using customer KMS where possible.
[06:40] Victor Zhao: Let's talk failure modes we need reported: percentages of hallucinations, critical intent failures, timeouts, and any misclassification leading to wrong triage.
[06:49] Carlos Nguyen: We'll add an automated test that flags critical intent failures and produces an artifact: a list of example failures with metadata (prompt id, generated result, expected result). That will be in the appendix and in the spreadsheet so you can triage easily.
[07:02] Maya Patel: For cost accounting, we can report estimated cost per 1M tokens for each variant, plus an estimated monthly run-cost under your projected traffic. That will be part of the cost guardrail gate.
[07:14] Victor Zhao: Good. If a variant meets correctness but exceeds cost guardrail, is that an automatic fail?
[07:19] Maya Patel: We'll present it as a soft-fail. The rubric will indicate hard failures (safety/critical intent miss, unmitigated PHI leakage) vs conditional fails (cost, slightly elevated latency) with recommended mitigations. The final decision is up to ClearSight sign-offs.
[07:33] [00:07:34] Speaker 1: yeah, makes sense.
[07:36] Carlos Nguyen: Operational notes — we'll collect per-run GPU metrics (util %, mem used), process logs, and the KV cache hit rates. That'll help explain variance. Sometimes the KV cache is mis-transcribed in notes; again we call it KV cache not K-V cash.
[07:51] Ben Carter: one more technical — do you support quantized int8 runs? We want to see that for cost reduction experiments.
[07:57] Carlos Nguyen: yes, we'll run quantized variants where possible and note any quality delta. We'll include the quantization profile in the appendix.
[08:06] Priya Singh: Are there any legal / procurement artifacts we should expect to get during the POC?
[08:11] Maya Patel: For the POC we typically share a scoped statement of work and a mutual NDA if not already in place. For Dedicated/private deployments there may be an MSA later.
[08:20] Victor Zhao: For reporting cadence — how will we present interim results? Daily status in the shared spreadsheet or a mid-week short readout?
[08:27] Maya Patel: We'll do a daily tab updates during active runs and a short daily stand (10 minutes) if you want; otherwise we'll run and deliver a consolidated report at the end. We'll do a short run notification before each major run.
[08:39] Lena Morris: Ok. One point on metrics — please normalize latency by tokens (ms/token) for the long-form summarization workloads.
[08:47] Carlos Nguyen: good call. We'll include ms/token along with p95 absolute latency.
[08:53] [00:08:54] Speaker 3: mhmm.
[08:55] Ben Carter: Any constraints on the prompt shape? Some prompts include attachments or multi-part inputs.
[09:00] Maya Patel: Capture multi-part inputs as concatenated JSON fields in the sample set; we'll document how we simulate attachments with representative tokenized content.
[09:11] Carlos Nguyen: I'll add that to the runbook template.
[09:15] Maya Patel: Alright let's walk through a sample go/no-go rubric row so everyone sees the format. (reads) Metric: Critical intent pass rate. Threshold: >=92% on labeled pack. Owner: Product/Customer. If fail: No-Go. Evidence required: labeled pack results + 10 failing examples.
[09:36] Victor Zhao: That format should work. Next — performance row. Metric: p95 latency under baseline concurrency. Threshold: <=450ms hard, 300ms stretch. Owner: Redwood infra. If fail: conditional - can we mitigate with autoscaling or dedicated capacity?
[09:52] Carlos Nguyen: For mitigation we can propose autoscale settings or a dedicated capacity bump; we'll include mitigation paths with estimated cost delta in the report.
[10:01] Priya Singh: Security row: PHI exfiltration detection. Threshold: zero events. Owner: Security. If fail: immediate stop and triage.
[10:10] Maya Patel: we'll instrument cross-checks on logs and a small rule-based detector for PHI tokens in generated outputs.
[10:18] [00:10:19] Speaker 1: okay.
[10:20] Maya Patel: Timeline recap: benchmark materials due 8/26, Redwood runs 8/25-8/27, internal review 8/28, final decision 8/29. Does that work?
[10:30] Victor Zhao: tight but doable. we'll aim for those dates.
[10:34] Ben Carter: Any preference for time-of-day for the runs? Ben: we prefer nights to minimize overlap with prod.
[10:38] Carlos Nguyen: we can run off-hours; we'll coordinate maintenance windows.
[10:42] [00:10:43] Speaker 2: all good.
[10:44] Maya Patel: Ok final few items — we'll send the benchmark runbook (template CSV, run commands, env vars), the decision rubric (table), and a reporting template (exec one-pager + spreadsheet). Also security appendix with SOC2 snapshot and KMS notes.
[10:56] Priya Singh: Please include encrypted transport confirmation and whether logs are accessible via a private endpoint.
[11:01] Carlos Nguyen: yes — we'll note that logs can be pushed to your S3 or an internal bucket behind VPC endpoints.
[11:08] Victor Zhao: Great. Anything else on reporting format? I want to ensure the exec one-pager has a single red/amber/green row for each gate.
[11:15] Maya Patel: We'll include an RAG summary plus the decision verbatim and the owner signature lines.
[11:21] Lena Morris: Sounds good.
[11:23] Maya Patel: Alright, we'll recap action items in the follow-up email. Thanks everyone — talk soon.
[11:30] Victor Zhao: Thanks.
[11:32] Priya Singh: Thanks, bye.
[11:34] [END]
transcription_issues: Occasional mis-transcription of technical terms (e.g., 'K-V cash' instead of 'KV cache')
Some speaker labels generic (Speaker 1/2/3) and may not map to exact attendees
Filler words and crosstalk included per typical Fireflies export
